    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Google has filed a patent application for a personalized television channel that uses artificial intelligence to generate shows starring the person watching.
    • Streaming platforms such as YouTube and Netflix already use viewing habits to recommend content, while companies have also started experimenting with broadcasting entirely AI-generated entertainment.
    • Google’s patent application, titled “Creating a Channel of Video Experiences Tailored to a User,” was originally filed on May 13, 2025, before being published by the US Patent and Trademark Office on November 19, 2026.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Google has filed a patent application for a personalized television channel that uses artificial intelligence to generate shows starring the person watching.

    Streaming platforms such as YouTube and Netflix already use viewing habits to recommend content, while companies have also started experimenting with broadcasting entirely AI-generated entertainment.

    Google’s patent application, titled “Creating a Channel of Video Experiences Tailored to a User,” was originally filed on May 13, 2025, before being published by the US Patent and Trademark Office on November 19, 2026.

    First spotted by Patentlyze, the application describes a feature called “My Channel” that would appear within a television app and offer a selection of videos created specifically for individual viewers.

    The system would use information including a person’s viewing history, location, language settings, and demographic data to determine what kinds of reveals they might enjoy.

    Google could then use photographs to create a digital avatar of the viewer and replicate their voice, allowing them to star in everything from romantic comedies to science fiction adventures.

    In a recent development, one example included in the filing describes how the system could generate a video starring someone who had recently watched cricket highlights. The viewer could appear in the stands during the Cricket World Cup or interact with one of their favorite players.

    Recent findings suggest that users wouldn’t necessarily have to request fresh content, either. The application outlines a scheduling system that could automatically generate videos on a weekly, monthly, or yearly basis. It also describes a mechanism for inserting advertisements into the generated content.

    Google now lets anyone make & use their own Android apps using AI.

    Newly introduced Microsoft patent could use AI to alter speech and lip movements in real time.

    YouTube tests prompt-based custom feeds that let you control your homepage.

    According to recent reports, however, Google has not declared plans to launch the feature. According to Patentlyze, a patent examiner has issued a final rejection of the application, although the company can still amend its claims or appeal the decision.

    The filing comes as AI-generated programming has already made its way onto streaming platforms, with Roku introducing a television channel dedicated to broadcasting AI-generated content around the clock.

    #116531. Bambu Lab P3C Review: A more affordable tool changer

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Tomshardware ↗ Open Full Page

    Bambu Lab P3C Review: A more affordable tool changer

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2694 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomshardware

    ⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, the Bambu Lab P3C is the lower-cost little brother of the H3C.
    • Works with multiple materials and nozzle sizes in the same print.
    • In a recent development, why you can trust Tom's Hardware Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, the Bambu Lab P3C is the lower-cost little brother of the H3C. It has the same type of tools and outstanding TPU printing process as its larger sibling, but drops the heated chamber, filament dryer, and automatic filament loading. If you want an upgradable tool changer on a more manageable budget, the P3C is a great place to start.

    Works with multiple materials and nozzle sizes in the same print.

    Works with almost all spool types.

    Changing tools is a pain, literally.

    In a recent development, why you can trust Tom's Hardware Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.

    Bambu Lab didn’t even tease the arrival of the new P3C, a smaller, more budget-friendly version of the H3C, which retails at roughly half the price. In fact, this post might be the first time you’ve heard more than just a rumor about the tool changer’s mysterious little brother.

    The Bambu Lab P3C combo is a tool changer with room for seven tools and a 256 x 256 x 260mm build volume, roughly the same as the P2S. It ships as either a five-tool unit, with two empty slots for later customization, or as a seven-tool “multi-material combo” with six 1.75mm tools and one 2.85mm tool. Bambu is bringing back old school 2.85mm filament in the form of super squishy TPU 75A.

    The five-tool unit is priced at $1,149, while the seven-tool is launching at $1,299.

    It offers the same excellent TPU printing process for both standard and phat TPU and has rapidly joined the select group of send it and forget it printers in my fleet. I’ve had very few failures, even when printing more technical filaments.

    Industry observers note that the P3C is not quite as tall as the H3C, but it does require almost 4ft (1,212 mm) of vertical space for the AMS lid to fully open. So initiative accordingly and have a good space picked out in advance.

    According to recent reports, bambu’s most annoying cost-saving measure took the A right out of AMS. There’s no motor of any sort in the AMS 3P, leaving you to manually load and unload the filament all the way to the nozzle. The process takes a long time if you are loading all of the filament slots. The upside of not having powered rollers is that the AMS 3P will run almost any 1kg or smaller spool without issue.

    In a recent development, the printer can run different-sized nozzles from .2 mm to .8 mm, and has an optional 2.85 mm TPU filament tool. The FlexFeed extruder with Active Grip Control just pushes whatever filament it’s asked to while changing on the fly. It may be the best extruder I’ve reviewed, however, the printer as a whole is not quite what we need for the best 3D printers of 2026.

    Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.

    256 x 256 x 260 mm (10.07 x 10.07 x 10.23 inches).

    330 x 320 x 325 mm (12.99 x 12.59 x 12.79 inches).

    PLA/TPU/ABS/ASA/PA/PC/PET/Fiber reinforced.

    PLA/TPU/ABS/ASA/PA/PC/PET/PPS/Fiber reinforced (up to 350 degrees).

    PEI textured spring steel sheet (110 degrees).

    PEI textured spring steel sheet (120 degrees).

    413 x 538 x 925 mm (16.25 x 21.18 x 36.4 in).

    493 x 571 x 1016 mm (19.40 x 22.48 x 40 inches).

    Industry observers note that the Bambu Lab P3C comes with five .4mm tools preinstalled in the bottom of the AMS 3P. Also included are a toolkit and cables needed to assemble the printer, along with quick start guides for both the printer and AMS 3P, and a few spare parts. It does not come with a USB memory stick, which is needed for recording time lapses.

    We received the multi-material combo for review, which came with five tools installed, plus two additional tools I had to set up myself (one 1.75mm and one 2.85mm), along with several spools of PLA Palette and 2.85mm TPU 75A.

    The P3C is missing several perks of the bigger H3C in order to save costs and keep the price reasonable. The most disappointing is the lack of a motor to drive the filament spools. This makes the “A” in the AMS 3P questionable, as you are forced to manually feed the filament all the way to the nozzle, as well as handle retraction when unloading.

    The AMS 3P also does not come with a filament drier, although an optional 75C dryer will be available for $159.90.

    According to recent reports, the basic Bambu Lab P3C comes standard with only five tools and is expandable to seven. The Swaptek system keeps the cooling fans and extruder on the toolhead, with each tool having its own filament path, heater, and a hardened steel nozzle. When printing, the idle tools are preheated, allowing for extremely fast tool swaps.

    The nozzles on each tool can be swapped out with different sizes, and multiple sizes can be used in the same print.

    Bambu Lab will also release tools for cutting, drawing, debossing, and foil transfer in the future.

    The Bambu Lab P3C supports printing TPU with a bypass port on all filament slots except 2 and 6, which allows TPU to skip the tube, reducing friction. If you have the optional 2.85mm tool, you can mount it to any slot with a bypass.

    Please note that the 2.85mm tool has a wider filament path – it's not just the nozzle tip that changes dimensions.

    The tools dock on a rack in front of the printer which retracts after each tool change, allowing for a clear view of the build plate.

    Industry observers note that the Flexfeed extruder is impressive. It switches from 1.75mm to 2.85mm filament on the fly and uses what Bambu Lab calls Active Grip Control with feedback from the extruder motor.

    Like the H3C, there are magnetic covers on the left and right sides of the AMS and a front cover that attaches in slots to allow easy access to the chamber for maintenance. The front cover is a bit tricky, and you need to lift the AMS up to get it free. For this reason, I didn’t bother to secure the AMS to the base of the printer. You really need to remove that front panel to change out the tools.

    Changing tools is one of the few frustrating things about the Bambu Lab P3C (or the H3C, as it’s the same process). There is very little room to work, and there are sharp plastic edges that left me bloodied on one occasion. I would suggest picking your favorite configuration and leaving it there if you can.

    The AMS is massive and requires a lot of additional vertical space to fully open the lid to get at the spools. Bambu Lab recommends a clearance of 1,212 mm or almost four feet from the base in order to open the lid. Surprisingly, this smaller P3C is only 3.58 inches shorter than the major H3C. With the printer sitting on a standard countertop, a step-stool will be mandatory equipment for most people. Bambu offers a rolling cart for the H3C that puts the printer at a more manageable height, and I would highly recommend getting it for the P3C.

    Industry observers note that the base unit of the Bambu Lab P3C looks similar to the P and X series printers, with a plastic outer frame and a steel chassis. The build plate is a standard 256 x 256 mm, with 260 mm available on the Z-axis. The P3C does not have active chamber heating, but being enclosed with a max of 300C on the nozzle and 110C on the bed, it has the ability to print many of the more common technical filaments. The chamber is ventilated with HEPA and active carbon filtration.

    Industry observers note that the 3D printer has a great camera, which is used for AI detection and monitoring using the Bambu Handy app and the device page of Bambu Slicer. The camera can produce time-lapses of your prints but does require a USB memory stick to store them.

    Recent findings suggest that the Bambu Lab P3C and AMS 3P ship in separate boxes but are almost fully assembled. After removing the packaging, there are two screws holding the dock retainers that need to be removed and 6 screws securing the bed in place.

    There is a helpful reminder to do this when the printer is first turned on. AMS 3P is mounted on top of the printer and requires a good deal of vertical space. There are four screws to attach the AMS 3P to the printer, but I left these off since the front panel of the AMS is easier to remove when you can tip the AMS back a little.

    The individual tools attach to the dock magnetically and must be placed manually, which can take a little fiddling to get used to.

    The touch screen attaches to the front of the printer without tools, and the ribbon cable to connect it is just long enough to work.

    It has been revealed that the Bambu Lab P3C levels its bed as part of its initial calibration and again at the start of every print. The system works perfectly.

    The Bambu Lab P3C does not have auto-loading, as there is no motor.

    When loading multiple upcoming filaments for a print, the process can take a while and is very hands-on. When using normal 1.75 mm filament, the material is pushed into the orange tube in the AMS when called for by the printer.

    When using TPU, either 1.75mm or 2.85 filament, drop the filament into a slot with a bypass port in the bottom and drag it by hand to the tool. The normal Bowden tube must be removed from the tool and clipped to the side. When running 1.75mm TPU a short piece of bowden tube must be inserted into the tool to help feed the filament correctly. The 2.85mm TPU doesn’t need the short tube and can feed directly.

    The printer has a helpful filament guide to walk you through the loading operation.

    Bambu Lab-branded filament with RFID tags will automatically enter the filament type and color. Other brands must be entered manually via the printer’s touchscreen.

    Unloading filament is the reverse of loading. You’ll need to manually retract material once it is cut by the printer. There is a batch unloading command that will allow you to wait until all of the selected filaments have been cut.

    In a recent development, bambu Studio is based on PrusaSlicer and its predecessors. New for the P3C and the H3C is the ability to mix different tool sizes. It is one of the best slicers available with good filament mapping, control and print monitoring, with access to Makerworld, Bambu Lab’s file sharing service.

    It has been revealed that the P3C does not come with filament samples. Bambu Lab sent a few spools of their latest PLA Palette and 2.85mm 75A TPU to try. Be sure to check out our best filaments for 3D printing to fill up your AMS 3P.

    It has been revealed that this print of Carl and Donut from the Dungeon Crawler Carl book series took 15 hours and 35 minutes to print using a .16mm layer height for smooth detail. I used the default settings, but slowed the outer walls to 65mm/s. The print is exceptionally good, though the supports left a few marks under horizontal areas like the arms and shin. Normally I’d tilt a model this back 45 degrees to save time and support, but the fin on this particular model is vexing and would have added an hour to the print time and another 10g of support.

    This is printed in seven colors of PLA, maxing out the P3C slots. Polymaker HT-PLA Pro White, Prusament Galaxy Black and Galaxy Silver PLA, Elegoo PLA Brown and Silk Red, Inland Bone White, and Matterhacker’s Purple MH Build Series PLA.

    It has been revealed that printing with seven colors allows you more creative freedom when printing complex models. Though the brown did a lot of heavy lifting on this print, I think the P3C really captured Carl nicely.

    I tried some of Bambu Lab’s matte PETG on a Cute Blue Jay from Makerworld. Since the model prints best straight up and down, and requires pretty extensive supports, I used a scrap of Prusa Lipstick Red PLA as an interface layer.

    Industry observers note that using a .16mm layer height, the print took 8 hours and 55 minutes running at a little under 100mm/s on average. The matte PETG makes the model look like it was painted. This is printed in black, white and baby blue matte PETG and the supports came off with no residue what so ever.

    Sources indicate that though the P3C doesn’t get hot enough to print PPS, it does print most PA, PC, and PET filaments very well. I printed a spool and a half of Sunlu Easy PA, making all of the mechanical parts for two radio-controlled Death Racers. Initially, I made just a few items per plate, but with just a little glue stick, the bed adhesion was so good that I felt comfortable loading up the plates as full as possible and had zero failures. All were printed with a .2mm layer height and slowed to 100mm/s by me in the slicer. Other than a tiny bit of stringing, the parts are perfect mechanically.

    The Bambu Lab P3C’s HEPA filter does a good job filtering the stinkier filaments like ABS and ASA. I printed this wire holding vice using Fusion ABS matte ionized cobalt black and Prusa lipstick red ASA.

    This is printed with a .2 mm layer height and an average print speed of 120mm/s. The entire print took a little less than 2 hours and 3 minutes, and the parts fit together perfectly.

    With the H3C and now the P3C, I have seen the future of printing with TPU. The AMS 3P bypass ports are just the ticket for printing soft materials.

    Sources indicate that I printed several plates of treads for my RC Death Racer project. Normally, I print these a few at a time to limit the fallout from print failures, but this proved unnecessary. I ran 48 treads in Bambu Lab Cyan 2.85mm TPU 75A and another 48 using Bambu Lab 90A TPU. Both prints used a .2mm layer height and were limited to 100 mm/s in the slicer. The 75A print finished a little quicker at 19 hours 10 minutes, with the 90A filament taking 19 hours and 40 minutes.

    Both are terrific prints with no stringing at all and zero failures.

    The P3C can print almost any filament I own beautifully. It lacks a few creature comforts like auto-loading, filament drying (which can be upgraded), and a heated chamber. It’s also tall enough to require a step stool to load those back filament slots.

    The Bambu Lab P3C is best for anyone who wants poop-free multicolor, multi-material printing without paying H3C money. I highly recommend it for anyone who looks to print a lot of TPU and doesn’t need that larger build plate. If you can live without the automatic feeding you normally get from a Bambu printer, then the money you’ll save in filament is worth the hassle.

    Industry observers note that this machine gives you most of the advantages of the Bambu Lab H3C at roughly half the $2,499 price tag. The open-source four-color Snapmaker U1 is still worth it right now while it’s on sale for $699. Another option is the Creality K3, which is another four-color tool changer with a similar build size for $849.

    Industry observers note that denise Bertacchi is a Contributing Writer for Tom’s Hardware US, covering 3D printing. Denise has been crafting with PCs since she discovered Print Shop had clip art on her Apple IIe. She loves reviewing 3D printers because she can mix all her passions: printing, photography, and writing.

    In a recent development, for Democrats eyeing the White House, President Donald Trump’s coziness with tech executives was already a potent target even before he successfully pressured Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive.Now his extraordinary intervention has crystallized their concerns about the growing power of artificial intelligence companies and his blending of government and business interests.Huang had lost his job because of extramarital affairs, including one with a Chinese businesswoman suspected of working as a spy for Beijing. Eleven days later, Nvidia’s board put him back in charge.Although Democrats lack a unified vision for how to handle the proliferation of artificial intelligence, the episode was an opportunity for them to speak largely in unison as they called Huang’s return a threat to national security and described Trump’s role as corrupt.Nvidia’s decision sends a message “that the national security of this country is not as crucial as your relationship with President Trump,” said Sen. Ruben Gallego, an Arizona Democrat considering a White House campaign, in an interview with The Associated Press.“We also have to figure out how corporate America doesn’t take a bad lesson from this, and thinks that somehow it’s OK for them to evade national security for the purposes of just selling more,” Gallego said.Nvidia is under scrutiny over whether it’s complying with U.S. restrictions on the export of its most advanced semiconductors to China and their use by Chinese tech firms.The manufacturer’s share price dropped sharply during Huang’s brief absence, dragging down the broader stock market to one of its worst weeks since the 2008 financial crisis, before recovering with Monday’s announcement of his reinstatement. Trump argues that Huang’s leadership at Nvidia is necessary Still euphoric over their sweeping midterm victories, many ambitious Democrats are still feeling around for the right message on artificial intelligence, which carries both promise and peril as it becomes increasingly intertwined with the economy, infrastructure and daily life.Trump’s intervention put a spotlight on his own financial stake in the company, which his latest financial disclosure report indicates was worth at least $12.5 million at the end of 2025, and on the millions of dollars Huang contributed to Trump’s ballroom project.Writing on social media that “rules should apply to everyone,” California Rep. Ro Khanna noted that “the rich & powerful, like Jensen, do not get to evade export controls or accountability just because it props up the stock price.”Trump worried that Huang’s ouster was not only tanking the stock market but also risked putting the U.S. behind Beijing in the race for tech dominance.“I’m doing it for the country,” Trump said on CNBC.Huang’s reinstatement reinforced the message, which many Democrats delivered in the midterms, that the system is rigged against average Americans, said Sacha Haworth, founder and CEO of The Tech Oversight Project and a former aide to Democrats. Substantial tech leaders can be a powerful foil.“They are the most unlikeable men in America, and yet it seems like the system is working very well for them,” Haworth said. “The news this week just reinforced that idea. So the mission that Democrats have now is to continue to prove to voters that they are fighting against this corrupt system, against the influence of tech CEOs and on behalf of Americans.”Nvidia’s board and Trump himself left no ambiguity over who drove the decision.It was based on input from “senior levels of the United States government,” Nvidia said in a press release announcing Huang’s return.Trump said in an interview with CNBC that “I spoke to them, let me just put it that way. And I convinced them.” Democratic candidates see corruption, security risks Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro tied Huang’s reinstatement to “the sheer corruption and weakness” of the president, calling it “another example of the dangerous combination governing this country: a rigged system that protects those at the very top no matter what, and a corrupt White House that cannot be trusted to put the economic well-being and safety of American families first.”Sen. Elissa Slotkin of Michigan said that Trump’s pressure campaign made clear that, to the president, “making money is more important than America’s national security or the rule of law.”Slotkin, a former CIA analyst, added, “If ever there was an glitch that deserved national security oversight, it’s this one.”And Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker drew a comparison between Huang’s reinstatement and Democrats’ broad wins in this month’s midterm elections, calling the CEO’s return an example of “the greed and lack of accountability that the country just rejected.”Pritzker urged Democrats “to speak with one voice and not be afraid to fight the Trump administration,” saying Trump and Vice President JD Vance “will move mountains for tech billionaires.” —Jonathan J.     #116527. What is Model Routing in AI?

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1962 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sitepoint ↗ Open Full Page

    What is Model Routing in AI?

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1962 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sitepoint

    ⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.
    • In a recent development, "Do you know the closest ATM?" and "I was charged twice, the refund never arrived, and now my card is blocked" are both customer messages.
    • According to recent reports, model routing fixes that.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

    Weekly. Free. One click to leave.

    7 Day Free Trial. Cancel Anytime.

    In a recent development, "Do you know the closest ATM?" and "I was charged twice, the refund never arrived, and now my card is blocked" are both customer messages. Most AI apps send both to the same large model and pay large-model prices for each one.

    According to recent reports, model routing fixes that. A router looks at each request and sends it to the cheapest model that can handle it, and keeps the expensive model for the requests that need it.

    According to recent reports, in this guide we'll cover what model routing is, how routers decide, and what it saves. Then we'll build a small router in about 60 lines of JavaScript and run it over 200 customer messages. At one setting it matched a large model's accuracy for about a third of the cost. At another it came within a point and a half for 89% less.

    In a recent development, model routing in AI is the practice of sending each request to the model best suited to it, instead of sending every request to one model. A router sits between your app and a pool of models, reads each request, and picks a model based on what you care about: cost, speed, or quality.

    You'll also see it called AI model routing, LLM routing, or LLM model routing. They all mean the same thing. The pool might be a small and a large model from one provider, or models from several providers behind one API.

    The idea rests on one observation: most requests are easy. A small model answers them as well as a large one, in a fraction of the time and for a fraction of the price. The router's whole job is finding the hard ones.

    The diagram below indicates a typical AI model routing architecture.

    In a recent development, model routing works in three steps: the router reads the request, decides which model should answer it, and forwards the request to that model. The middle step is where routers differ. Routing tools decide which model to use in one of four ways.

    Recent findings suggest that rule-based routing uses rules you write by hand. Requests from free-plan users go to a small model. Anything tagged as code goes to a coding model. Prompts over a certain length go to a model with a bigger context window. It's simple, predictable, and free to run, but the rules only know what you thought of in advance.

    Intelligent model routing uses a model to make the decision. A small, fast classifier reads each request and predicts which model in the pool will answer it well. You'll also see it called smart or dynamic model routing.

    Sources indicate that two more terms come up here. Task-aware routing picks a model by the kind of job, like summarising, coding, or answering a support question. Context-aware routing also looks at what surrounds the request, like the conversation so far, the user, or the tools available.

    Recent findings suggest that the big platforms work this way. Microsoft describes its Foundry model router as "a trained language model" that picks a model for each prompt in real time. Google indicates Gemini Notebook uses its new Decisions API as a real-time router, serving everyday queries with up to 40% lower latency. I've tested the Google Decisions API against Jev on the same messages we'll use below.

    Recent findings suggest that cascade routing tries the cheapest model first and only moves up when the answer isn't good enough. The usual test is confidence: if the cheap model is sure, keep its answer. If it isn't, send the request to a stronger model. It's also called confidence-based routing, and it's what we'll build below.

    A cascade needs no separate classifier, because the first model's own confidence does the routing. The trade-off is that escalated requests pay for two models and wait for both.

    Sources indicate that fallback routing is about staying up, not saving money. If a model times out, hits a rate limit, or its provider has an outage, the router sends the request to the next model on a list. Most production routers combine fallbacks with one of the three methods above.

    The main benefits of model routing in AI systems are lower cost, faster responses, and fewer outages, without giving up quality on the hard requests.

    According to recent reports, we'll build a cascade router for a job every support tool has: sorting customer messages. Each message gets one of ten labels, like atm support or request refund.

    The test set is 200 messages from Banking77, a public set of banking support messages: ten labels, 20 messages each. They're the same 200 messages from my zero shot classification test, which is where the single-model numbers below come from.

    Industry observers note that put both keys in a .env file and run the examples with node --env-file=.env. It's the same setup as in my guide to getting a YouTube API key.

    Create router.mjs. The first function sends the message to Jev with one multiple-choice question, and returns the label Jev picked along with its confidence:.

    Confidence runs from 0 to 1. When nearly all the probability sits on one label, it's close to 1. When Jev is torn between two labels, it drops.

    Industry observers note that the second function asks Claude Opus 5.5 the same question. The output_config block limits the answer to one of our labels, so there's no free text to parse. SitePoint's guide to LLM structured output with JSON Schema explains how that works.

    The router itself is about a dozen lines:.

    Recent findings suggest that if Jev is at least 80% confident, its answer goes straight back. If not, Claude answers instead. And if Claude fails, the router falls back to Jev's answer, because a shaky answer beats an error page.

    Try it on an easy message and a harder one:.

    Jev was sure about the lost card. On the ATM question it leaned towards card acceptance with a confidence of 0.64, so the router asked Claude, which got it right.

    Because cheap, strong, and threshold are options, the same function routes between any two models.

    Sources indicate that model routing reduces AI costs by keeping easy requests on a cheap model and paying for the expensive one only when it's needed. Here's what that looked like on our 200 messages, starting with each model on its own:.

    Opus gets six more messages right out of 200, and costs more than 120 times as much.

    Now the router, at four confidence thresholds:.

    In a recent development, speed improved too. At the 0.8 threshold, the messages Jev kept came back in a median of 227 ms. The ones that escalated took about 2.1 seconds, because they waited for both models.

    A note on method: I ran every message through both models once and saved the answers, then replayed the router over them at each threshold. That's how you compare thresholds without paying for the same test four times.

    Then I ran the router live to check. At 0.95 it scored the same 95.0% and sent 61 messages to Opus. At 0.8 it scored 93.5% and sent 20, a point under the replay. Two answers moved: one of Jev's confidence scores landed at 0.82 instead of 0.78, just over the line, and Opus changed its answer on one message. Scores near the threshold shift a little between runs, so leave yourself a margin.

    The choice of cheap model matters less than you'd think. With Google's Gemini Decision 1 in first place instead of Jev, a 0.7 threshold reached the same 95% for US$0.28 per 1,000 messages.

    Model routing can cost a little quality, and the threshold decides how much. In our test the gap to Opus ranged from nothing at 0.95 to two points at 0.7.

    According to recent reports, the loss comes from one place: answers the cheap model got wrong while feeling sure. At the 0.8 threshold, Jev kept five wrong answers because its confidence was above the line. Opus got four of those five wrong as well, so only one was a real loss: "Do all ATMs take this card?", which Jev filed under card acceptance with a confidence of 0.91.

    It has been revealed that escalating isn't risk-free either. On one message, Jev had the right label with a confidence of 0.44, and Opus overruled it with the wrong one.

    Recent findings suggest that to optimize costs using AI model routing, measure first, route second, and keep measuring. These six steps cover LLM model routing cost optimization for any pair of models:.

    The return is easy to estimate once you know the split. If nine in ten requests stay on a model that costs 1% as much, the bill drops by about 89%, which is what we measured.

    Several inference providers have multi-model routing built in, and most AI gateway platforms support model routing too, so you don't have to write your own. As of November 2026, these are the top model routing solutions for AI apps. Each name links to the tool's model routing docs:.

    Hosted model routing platforms for large language models decide for you, which is the fastest way to start. A hand-built router like ours takes more work, but you choose the signal and you can see why every request went where it did.

    It has been revealed that an LLM router is the component that does model routing for large language models. It can be a function in your own code, like the one in this guide, a hosted model such as Microsoft Foundry's model router, or a feature of an AI gateway.

    Smart model routing is another name for intelligent model routing: a model, not a hand-written rule, decides where each request goes. Dynamic model routing means the same thing.

    In a recent development, the ROI of AI model routing depends on how much of your traffic a cheaper model can handle. In our test, a 0.8 threshold kept 89.5% of messages on the cheap model and cut the cost per 1,000 messages from US$1.96 to US$0.22, for about a point of accuracy. The build was about 60 lines of code.

    OpenRouter's auto model routing works through its Auto Router. You set the model to openrouter/auto, and a decision model picks a model and a reasoning effort for each request. You pay the standard rate of whichever model it selects, with no extra fee.

    In a recent development, openClaw model routing is a primary model plus an ordered list of fallbacks. In the OpenClaw model routing configuration you set agents.defaults.model.primary and agents.defaults.model.fallbacks, and an agent can override the fallback list. When a model fails, OpenClaw first rotates auth profiles on the same provider, then moves to the next model on the list, as its model failover docs describe. That makes it fallback routing, not cost-based routing.

    An AI gateway simplifies model routing by putting every model behind one API, one set of keys, and one place for logs. Your app calls the gateway, and the routing rules live in config instead of code, so changing a model doesn't need a deploy.

    Recent findings suggest that mid-stream failover is when a router switches models after a streamed response has already started, because the first model failed partway through. It's the hardest kind of failover, because the user has already seen part of an answer. Many routers only fail over before the first token arrives and return an error after that, so check what your gateway does.

    #116525. BYD’s latest car has a disappearing steering wheel—because it can

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1688 w)

    EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fastcompany ↗ Open Full Page

    BYD’s latest car has a disappearing steering wheel—because it can

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1688 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fastcompany

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • BYD just killed the steering wheel as we know it.
    • Sources indicate that BYD just killed the steering wheel as we know it.
    • It only needs 10 seconds, then puff, the wheel is gone and the dashboard is clean.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    BYD just killed the steering wheel as we know it. Permanently bolted in front of the driver, it’s a fundamental part of the car. Unless you’re BYD. The Chinese automaker’s new six-seat plug-in hybrid SUV features a disappearing steering wheel that folds itself into a dashboard compartment at the push of a button. It only needs 10 seconds, then puff, the wheel is gone and the dashboard is clean. The driver suddenly has about 10 more inches of legroom. BYD bills it as the world’s first in a production car. Aside from race cars with their pop-in and pop-out steering wheels, nobody has ever seen anything like this. The magic wheel comes only with the $49,400 Folding Smart Cabin trim of the Tai 9, a model from BYD’s sub-brand Fang Cheng Bao. During the November 19 launch, Fang Cheng Bao’s general manager, Xiong Tianbo, noted that another carmaker floated a folding wheel back in 2016. It wasn’t possible at the time. “It has always been difficult to bring into mass production,” Xiong said. The reason, he explained, is that in a traditional car, “a mechanical steering column connects the steering wheel and the wheels,” adding “that one column limits the imagination for the entire driver’s space.” [Image: BYD] The Tai 9 doesn’t need a hard steering column because it uses a steer-by-wire system. Rather than mechanically pushing the road wheels to a new angle through a shaft, a rack, and a pair of tie rods, the system uses a new folding steering wheel that works like a game controller. Turn it, and electronic sensors “read” the movement, sending an electronic signal to the motors that actually turn the road wheels. The same trim also gets brake-by-wire, which swaps the brakes’ mechanical link for electronic signals, too. This is similar to the fly-by-wire technology that modern fighter airplanes use. Rather than directly driving heavy hydraulic systems, the pilot uses a joystick similar to a computer controller. It sends impulses that get interpreted by a computer, which in turn operates the mechanics of the airplane to make it change direction in the air. BYD indicates it has five layers of redundancy covering sensing, control, actuation, communications, and power supply.     Rockstar is turning GTA 6’s in-game trading cards into real collectibles

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Rockstar Games has partnered with Panini to release real-life GTA 6 trading cards based on the collectibles players can find scattered throughout Leonida.
    • There’s no shortage of things to collect in Grand Theft Auto 6, with Rockstar taking a page out of Red Dead Redemption 2’s book by including hundreds of trading cards for players to hunt down.
    • There are 480 cards across 18 different sets, ranging from fictional sports stars to comic book characters and nightclub dancers, with players able to sell their rare finds at pawn shops for some extra cash.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Rockstar Games has partnered with Panini to release real-life GTA 6 trading cards based on the collectibles players can find scattered throughout Leonida.

    There’s no shortage of things to collect in Grand Theft Auto 6, with Rockstar taking a page out of Red Dead Redemption 2’s book by including hundreds of trading cards for players to hunt down.

    There are 480 cards across 18 different sets, ranging from fictional sports stars to comic book characters and nightclub dancers, with players able to sell their rare finds at pawn shops for some extra cash.

    Now, just days after GTA 6’s record-breaking launch, Rockstar is giving collectors a chance to rip open packs in real life.

    Recent findings suggest that grand Theft Auto VI official trading cards, coming soon from @PaniniAmerica and @RockstarGames. pic.twitter.com/H1VrYVXTm5.

    On November 24, Panini announced its partnership with Rockstar Games to produce the first officially licensed Grand Theft Auto trading card collection, set to launch in December 2026.

    Dubbed the GTA VI: Sports Trading Card Collection, the set will recreate cards featuring fictional athletes and teams from Rockstar’s universe.

    According to Panini’s product listing, each hobby box will contain four packs of four cards, with collectors pulling an average of two Rookies, one Retro, one Illustrated, and four Special Silvers per box.

    Much like real-world sports cards, there will also be rare color variants and numbered parallels, including Bronze Legend cards limited to 49 copies, Silver Legends limited to 25, and coveted one-of-one Gold cards.

    It has been revealed that you just know all the down bad GTA 6 players who have fallen head over heels for goth stripper Vicki, will be clamoring for her card. However, the collection may be limited to sports cards for now.

    The collaboration is the latest example of Rockstar bringing its fictional world to life, having already created a real-life Grotti Cheetah worth £1 million and teamed up with the Miami Heat for Vice City merchandise.

    Panini has yet to announce pricing, an exact release date, or international availability, but considering how much money GTA 6 merchandise has already fetched on the resale market, those one-of-one cards could end up being worth a pretty penny.
